title: Does Shallow Alignment Persist After Instruction Fine-Tuning on Benign Data?

original_idea.problem: Whether benign fine-tuning specifically amplifies or deepens shallow alignment is unclear.
original_idea.direction: Fine-tune Llama-3-8B-Instruct on a benign coding dataset using LoRA, then re-run token-depth boundary experiment. Compare before/after ASR curves.
original_idea.why_it_matters: Many real deployments fine-tune aligned models on domain data. If benign fine-tuning makes alignment shallower, this is an underappreciated deployment risk.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: benign fine-tuning -> potential alignment depth change -> deployment risk characterization. Directly relevant to common deployment practices.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires LoRA fine-tuning on a coding dataset then running alignment depth experiments. Fine-tuning is advanced for beginner CS students in 30 hours. Needs familiarity with training pipelines.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: before/after ASR curve comparison. Clear methodology. The fine-tuning step adds work but the deliverable is well-defined.

novelty.reasoning: This question is well-studied. 'Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To!' (ICLR 2024) established that benign fine-tuning degrades alignment. 'The Geometry of Alignment Collapse' (arXiv:2602.15799, 2026) provides geometric analysis of how fine-tuning breaks safety. SafeMERGE (arXiv:2503.17239, 2025) and SALORA (ICLR 2025) propose mitigations for alignment degradation during LoRA fine-tuning. 'Narrow Fine-Tuning Erodes Safety Alignment' (arXiv:2602.16931, 2026) confirms the phenomenon in VLMs. The specific before/after ASR curve comparison using LoRA on Llama-3-8B-Instruct is a direct replication of well-established findings, with minimal novel contribution.
